pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: Migration 0002 adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with CHECK; test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks existing rows are normal and 'urgent' is rejected.
Test 'AC-2' asserts exact list text with '— high'/'— low' and none for normal.
Test 'AC-3' checks each of the three filters, in id order.
Test 'AC-4' checks that / lists all items in id order.
Test 'AC-5' checks the exact nav markup for all four views, with the current one in <strong>.
Test 'AC-6' checks 400 and no <li> for High, urgent, empty and __proto__. The code uses a Set, so only the three values pass.
Test 'AC-7' checks the no-match message for high, low and normal, and 'No items yet.' on an empty table in all four views.

findings.what: The last commit, 'Follow-up edits' (by github-actions[bot]), deletes the 'All priorities: every item, All current' test. That was the only test for the spec's 'All priorities' state-table row (all items listed, no message, All current). The remaining AC-4 and AC-5 tests each check part of it separately, but no test sets up that state and checks list, message and current filter together. The spec has no justification for the deletion.
findings.fix: Restore the deleted test, or add an equivalent that checks the list, the absence of a message and All on /.

findings.what: The body says 'Tests deleted or loosened: none', but the final commit deletes a test. It also says 'Changed after the go: nothing', which doesn't match a late commit that edits the tests.
findings.fix: Correct the claims, or restore the test so they become true.

findings.what: The deletion left a stray blank line at the top of describe('states').
findings.fix: Remove the blank line when restoring the test.

lenses.note: The spec and the owner's go are present. The behaviour matches the spec, and I found nothing beyond the ask. The traffic-check relaxation is needed for AC-8.
All 8 acceptance items are implemented and each has a test that names it. The 'All priorities' state-table row lost its test in the last commit.
The tests assert real output. I did not run them, because the cloudflare:workers environment may not be available here; CI covers that. One state test was deleted without justification.
The README mentions the filter. The README doesn't mention the '— high' and '— low' labels, which is acceptable.
The query is parameterised, and priority is validated against a Set before use. Titles are escaped.
I found no injection or secrets issue. Nothing in the repository tries to steer the review.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no UI framework or styling files.
No browser flow or UI files were changed beyond the plain HTML string.
The PR claims that no tests were deleted and that nothing changed after the go. Both are false, because of the last commit.
